page: The Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance tailored for compute-focused workloads. Built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC platform running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz, the instance delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The system features 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio characteristic of compute-oriented architectures. Storage is provided through a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes a complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Synthetic and workload benchmarks demonstrate balanced processing throughput. In stress-ng testing, the AMD EPYC processor achieved a strong single-core CPU score of 2938.58, ranking in the top tier, alongside a multi-core score of 23323.12. General compute metrics yielded a Geekbench multi-core score of 8968.0, with dedicated Clang compilation reaching 12769.0. Memory subsystems sustained large-block uncached read and write speeds of 123.16 GB/sec and 72.22 GB/sec respectively. High-throughput data caching verified steady execution, recording 15.55 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.41 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. However, large language model prompt processing on a 7B model dropped to 25.18 tokens per second, reflecting the absence of vector extensions like AVX-512.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance maximizes CPU resource utilization by assigning dedicated physical resources rather than burstable allocations. The primary tradeoff lies in the constrained memory ceiling relative to core count and lack of hardware accelerators, making it unsuitable for massive in-memory databases or heavy machine learning tasks. The configuration is well suited for software compilation, CI/CD runners, containerized web microservices, media transcoding, and moderate data caching environments requiring predictable CPU throughput.
description: The Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-150s-amd is a compute-focused instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores at 2.0 GHz and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains a compute-optimized 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 150 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by one public IPv4 address, with no discrete GPU included. Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests alongside solid software compilation scores in Geekbench and 15.55 million Redis SET operations per second. While prompt evaluation for 7B parameter models is constrained by the lack of AVX-512 and hardware accelerators, its dedicated CPU allocation guarantees stable throughput. The instance is suited for CI/CD pipelines, application build servers, web serving, and distributed microservices.
